subject: Silverpine discovery — pain points, goals, and SDK bridge plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@silverpine.ai>, Max Turner <max.turner@silverpine.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Silverpine discovery — pain points, goals, and SDK bridge plan

Hi Aisha / Max —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our end so we have a shared record and clear next steps. I kept this deliberately short — highlight items below and a proposed technical path for the integration.

Key pain points you mentioned
- Model latency variability in peak customer workflows (esp. multi-turn product support flows) — spikes to 1.6–2s per token are causing timeouts in your UI.
- Cost unpredictability when customers enable full-document reranking (long context + dense embeddings).
- Difficulty operationalizing function-calling at scale — current homegrown router can't easily shard calls between local models and cloud fallbacks.

Goals you want to achieve in the next 90 days
- Stable 99th percentile latency < 600ms for single-turn queries across 95% of traffic.
- A repeatable SDK path so product teams can use streaming + function-calling with minimal infra changes.
- A pilot to move rerank/embeddings to a batched, cached flow for cost reduction without regression in relevance.

Suggested integration approach (high level)
1) SDK bridge: we provide an adapter in v0.1 that mirrors your current client calls (same method names) and enables streaming with incremental tokens and function-call hooks. Minimal changes on your side — call signatures preserved.
2) Streaming + function calls: opt-in streaming endpoint with a two-phase commit for function-calls (stream tokens until call candidate, then call handler stub). We can instrument the SDK to emit metrics to your telemetry.
3) Embeddings/rerank: run embeddings offline for large corpora, use KD-tree for candidate generation, then run lightweight batched rerank on favored models. We'll suggest quantization profiles to cut VRAM and cost.
4) Fallthrough routing: start with hosted Redwood API for baseline, then transparent routing to Dedicated pool for high-throughput customers.

Action items / owners
- Redwood: deliver SDK adapter prototype (Jonas) — target EOW 2027-05-21.
- Silverpine: share a representative traffic sample and a small corpus for rerank eval (Aisha) — target 2027-05-18.
- Joint: set up a 60-minute technical working session to review the prototype and telemetry (Ben to coordinate) — suggested 2027-05-25.

Attachments: I attached a short integration checklist and a draft SOW with milestone placeholders.

If this looks right, I’ll start the SDK adapter and Ben will send a calendar invite for the working session.

Best,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: silverpine-integration-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), silverpine-sow-draft.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@silverpine.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Max Turner <max.turner@silverpine.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Silverpine discovery — pain points, goals, and SDK bridge plan

Thanks Jonas — this is great and captures our priorities. A couple of clarifications:

- The latency spikes happen most during concurrent document search + generation when customers request a rerank + function-call to an upstream CRM. The CRM latency is variable which exacerbates tail latency.
- For the embeddings corpus, we can provide a 50k-document slice and a held-out set for relevance checks.
- We’d like the SDK to preserve current retry semantics.

We’ll share the traffic snapshot and the corpus by 2027-05-18. Please call out any telemetry fields you need from our side (trace IDs, user cohort tags).

Also: Max asked whether Redwood supports canary routing by user cohort today (we discussed routing policies but want confirmation).

—Aisha

--
Aisha Khan
Head of Product, Platform | Silverpine AI
aisha.khan@silverpine.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@silverpine.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Silverpine discovery — pain points, goals, and SDK bridge plan

Aisha — thanks for the quick confirmation and the specifics. Short answers:
- Canary by cohort: yes, we can do cohort-based canary routing in the control plane; we’ll supply a few common rollout policies (percentage, header-based, user-id hash).
- Retry semantics: we’ll mirror your current client semantics in the adapter and expose config for backoff/timeout.
- Telemetry: please include trace IDs and an anonymized user_cohort tag; we’ll add fields for request_id, model_variant, batch_size, and latency_ms.

Given your timing, I’ll start the SDK adapter now. Ben — can you take the lead on the working-session invite and include an agenda (prototype demo + telemetry mapping + runbook for the pilot)?

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Silverpine discovery — pain points, goals, and SDK bridge plan

Looping in schedule + next steps. I’ll send a Doodle for the 60-minute working session and propose these agenda items:

3) Embeddings/rerank pilot design — 15m
4) Milestones + SOW review (draft attached) — 10m
